From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 11:21:00 +0200
Subject: RE: FW: Proposed MSA/Order Form redlines + DPA Annex mapping — action items

Steph / Ben — I've reviewed the BrightStream materials and drafted commentary + redlines in DPA_AnnexB_redline.docx and a short notes list below. Key points: 

- SCCs / Transfer basis: BrightStream has marked the Controller-Processor SCCs. We should accept C-P modules but add a fallback clause permitting temporary processing in non-EU regions for failover with 72 hours notice and documented risk assessment (proposed language included).

- Data residency: We can commit to EU primary residency for production workloads and a technical requirement to pin regions in the Order Form. However we should not represent absolute prohibition of failover — instead use "primary region: EU; failover to [designated regions] with notice and approval".

- Training carveout: Do NOT accept BrightStream's broad training carveout as drafted. Proposed compromise: allow training on de-identified/aggregated telemetry with an explicit ban on retention of raw PII; require documented de-identification process and annual attestation.

- Subprocessors: Counter to 30-day notification, propose 21-day notice for normal additions, 72-hour notice for security-critical subprocessors with an option for emergency onboarding with post-notice.

- KMS & keys: If customer requires KMS-managed keys, add an Exhibit in the Order Form for bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options; include an appendix for HSM/KMS integrations and estimated ops lead time (2-4 weeks).

I've added language snippets in the attached docx. I also flagged two terms I want product to confirm: (a) whether "pin to EU" can be strictly enforced for the pilot environment, and (b) whether training can be disabled via tenant-level setting. Can you confirm both?

Attaching: DPA_AnnexB_redline.docx

-Laura
Senior Counsel, Privacy | Redwood Inference

Claire — thanks for the patience. Please find attached our consolidated artifacts: Redwood_consolidated_DPA_matrix.xlsx (crosswalk + recommendations) and a proposed redline for the DPA Annex (DPA_AnnexB_redline.docx). Summary of the key positions pulled from legal: 

1) Data residency: Commit to EU primary residency for production; explicit Order Form pinning required for pilot. Failover allowed with 72 hours notice and risk assessment.
2) SCCs: C-P modules accepted with the fallback wording above.
3) Training carveout: We propose a restricted training clause — training allowed only on de-identified/aggregated telemetry with documented process + annual attestation.
4) Subprocessors: 21-day notice for normal additions; 72-hour notice for security-critical subprocessors; emergency onboarding allowed with post-hoc notice.
5) BYOK/KMS: We can support BYOK for enterprise customers; add Exhibit and project ops lead time.

Action items & timeline: 
- BrightStream: confirm whether pilot must absolutely prohibit any cross-region failover (reply requested by 2026-08-13).
- Redwood Product (cc'd): confirm whether pilot environment can be strictly pinned to EU (Ben: please advise by 2026-08-12).
- If BrightStream agrees to our compromise language we will circulate a countersigned Order Form + DPA package for procurement review by 2026-08-18.

Attachments: Redwood_consolidated_DPA_matrix.xlsx; DPA_AnnexB_redline.docx

If you'd like a 30-minute sync to walk through the matrix, I'm available tomorrow 10:00-12:00 CEST.
